name: Weerberg
kurzbeschreibung: Vibrant mountain village nestled on the sun-drenched slopes of the Inntal valley, offering expansive hiking trails, lush Almen, and the historic pilgrimage church Maria Tax.
beschreibung:
Überblick

The sunny mountain village of Weerberg is situated at an elevation of 882 metres above sea level on an expansive terrace overlooking the Lower Inn Valley within the Schwaz district, gracing the scenic slopes of the Tux Pre-Alps. Home to approximately 2,550 residents, this sprawling rural community comprises the sections of Außerweerberg, Mitterweerberg, and Innerweerberg, extending to alpine trailheads at Hausstatt and Innerst above 1,250 metres. Known as the 'Sun Village' (Sonnendorf), Weerberg enjoys above-average sunshine hours owing to its elevated south-facing aspect and commands sweeping vistas across the Inn Valley towards the Karwendel mountains. Steeped in living pastoral traditions, the village provides direct access to one of the most celebrated hiking and ski-touring domains in the Tux Alps.

Geschichte

Permanent settlement of the high plateau began during the High Middle Ages through pastoral clearing farms ('Schwaighöfe'). The village was officially documented around 1300, existing as an autonomous civic community since 1491. Weerberg boasts the unique cultural heritage of two complete parish churches: the Old Parish Church of Saints Peter and Paul was constructed between 1742 and 1752 on a glacial moraine hill by the renowned Tyrolean master builder Franz de Paula Penz, ranking among Tyrol's most iconic photographic landmarks. As the village expanded, the New Parish Church of the Immaculate Conception was built in Mitterweerberg between 1856 and 1872 as a monumental neo-Romanesque basilica featuring twin towers and Nazarene frescoes. Nearby stands the Rablhaus, a timber farmstead dating from the 16th century, now preserved as an acclaimed museum.

Anreise

Weerberg is reached via a scenic, well-maintained mountain road ascending from the Inn Valley. Motorists leave the Inntal Autobahn A12 at the Vomp/Schwaz or Wattens exits, proceed to Weer, and follow the Weerberg provincial road L300 climbing in wide panoramic curves onto the terrace and continuing to Hausstatt and Innerst. Rail travellers arrive via S-Bahn Tirol trains (lines S4 and S5) calling half-hourly at Pill-Vomperbach or Fritzens-Wattens stations, with long-distance rail links at Jenbach and Innsbruck Central Station. From Schwaz and Weer, regular services on VVT regional bus route 4125 travel up to Weerberg, serving all major hamlets as well as mountain trailheads at Hausstatt and Innerst.

Tipps

Visitors should explore both parish churches: the Old Church of St. Peter atop its panoramic knoll and the monumental twin-towered New Church in the village centre. Situated just below the historic churchyard, the award-winning Rablhaus Museum offers fascinating exhibitions on domestic folk religion, protective rituals, herbal remedies, and peasant heritage within an authentic smokehouse kitchen. For alpine hikers and ski mountaineers, the Innerst car park in the Nafing Valley serves as the primary gateway to the Weidener Hütte (1,799 m), an Alpine Club refuge offering routes across the historic Geiseljoch pass into the Zillertal or up the panoramic Rastkogel (2,762 m). From Hausstatt, the Gilfert (2,506 m) represents one of North Tyrol's premier viewpoints.
